notes: Identity assessment: the supplied canonical text is a full primary journal article, headed Journal of Experimental Psychology, VOL. XVIII, No. 6, DECEMBER, 1935, STUDIES OF INTERFERENCE IN SERIAL VERBAL REACTIONS, BY J. RIDLEY STROOP, pp. 643–662. Its provenance header identifies DOI 10.1037/h0054651, matching the assigned reference; title, author, date, pagination and Experiment 2 content independently agree. No PDF was supplied (source_pdf_path null), so no rendering was available. The assigned original contrast is identifiable from Experiment 2 and the p. 651 locator, independently of row order or numeric matching. Both printed effect candidates describe that contrast: 2.5 standard deviation units using NCWd variability and 4.35 using NC variability. Neither the neutral description nor the requested metric specifies the denominator, so no candidate is selected and target_match remains null. Table III reports time means, variability, raw differences, probable error and a reliability ratio, rather than a p value; pp. 650–652 contain no same-contrast p value or p bound. No p value is calculated from the reliability ratio. N, replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders; no N derivation performed.
